summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis was admitted after worsening left hip pain following a fall one week prior. Imaging confirmed left superior and inferior pubic rami fractures without displacement, managed conservatively with weight-bearing as tolerated and pain control using oxycodone. She also reported chronic abdominal pain and nausea, attributed to constipation from withholding lactulose; symptoms improved with reinitiation of her bowel regimen. Her cirrhosis remained stable without encephalopathy or decompensation. She was maintained on her home medications, including lactulose, rifaximin, spironolactone, and psychiatric drugs. Physical therapy cleared her for discharge home with a walker and home services. She was discharged with follow-up arranged in orthopedics and hepatology, advised to abstain from alcohol, and given a short course of oxycodone for pain.
problems: Major depressive affective disorder, single episode, unspecified
Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
